MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.
   C. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.
   D. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   D. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.

3. Best practice when working on Setting Text to Music: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Setting Text to Music.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Setting Text to Music.
   C. Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Setting Text to Music.

4. Best practice when working on Western Instruments: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Western Instruments.
   B. Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Western Instruments.
   D. Damage equipment used for Western Instruments.

5. Best practice when working on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   C. Damage equipment used for Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.

6. Best practice when working on Contemporary Songs from Kenya: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   B. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Songs from Kenya.
   D. Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Brown, pink, and gold
   B. Red, blue, and yellow
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Green, orange, and purple

8. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   D. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

9. Best practice when working on Kenyan Contemporary Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   B. Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Contemporary Songs.

10. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.
   D. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.

11. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software.: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Music Notation Software..
   C. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software..
   D. Refuse all feedback on Music Notation Software..

12. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. The ticket price
   B. The speed of the music
   C. Only the volume
   D. Only the costume

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Instrumental Transpositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Setting Text to Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Four-Part Harmony and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. A — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. C — Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. B — Practise Western Instruments with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. A — Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. D — Practise Contemporary Songs from Kenya with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. B — Red, blue, and yellow

8. B — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

9. B — Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. A — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. A — Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. B — The speed of the music

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rhythm; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Instrumental Transpositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Setting Text to Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Four-Part Harmony; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
